description: The eight stages of the backstory-driven hero creator (planning/character-backstory-creation.md sections 4.2 and 6) as data. Option cards are original DungeonFlux presentation aids, not rules: they can only spend the free choices of the standard build (background, class, ability order, skills, languages, alignment, kit, fighting style). Text is mature by default; text_restrained is given where the restrained rating must differ. Roll tables follow the dossier face rule (smallest die in 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 20 with n <= die, faces spread evenly).

signal_notation.weights: 1 nudge, 2 strong, 3 decisive for background and class; species and ability and skills and languages and tools are 1 or 2; alignment axis points are 1 or 2.
signal_notation.background: Weights on the four SRD carrier backgrounds (acolyte, criminal, sage, soldier). Custom backgrounds are reached through the trade, never by weight.
signal_notation.species: Weak lean on SRD species ids, only used to fill an unchosen species tile.
signal_notation.ability: Emphasis points on str dex con int wis cha (design 4.5).
signal_notation.skills: Leans for the class's own skill picks.
signal_notation.languages: Leans for the two free standard languages.
signal_notation.tools: Leans for a free tool choice (gaming set variant).
signal_notation.alignment: Axis points: law, chaos, good. Evil is never produced (design 4.7).
signal_notation.tags: Closed list in story_tags. Campaign story tags and location tags (design 7.1).

story_tags.meaning: Travel, caravans and the long way round.
The hidden side of a town.
Fire, flood and the night it happened.
Soldiers, skirmishes and what they leave.
Owing, being owed, and the weight of both.
Cold winters, harsh masters, long walks.
Someone is gone and must be found.
A name, a triumph, being seen.
A place or people worth defending.
Making amends or running from them.
A question that will not let go.
Something done that cannot be undone.
A long contest with one particular person.

hero_rows.note: Rows in the shape of the NPC dossier tables (id, speakers, text) for hero-only ids the picker needs and the dossier tables lack. Ids never collide with a dossier id. They are not listed in tables.json, so existing adventure revisions do not move. Third-person phrase text, as in the dossier.

origins.text: raised in a woodcutters' clearing where the trees were the nearest neighbours
brought up in a charcoal burners' hollow, black to the elbows from the age of six
born in the cistern lanes under a walled town, learning every dry way through
raised on tannery row, where the smell kept the watch away and the neighbours close

formative_events.text: was sold out by someone they trusted and has watched people's hands ever since
killed someone in an unfair fight and has never told the whole story
formative_events.text_restrained: hurt someone badly in an unfair fight and has never told the whole story

formative_events.text: watched a village burn from a hillside, too far away to help
formative_events.text_restrained: watched a village lost to fire from a hillside, too far away to help

wants.text: wants someone to answer for a wrong the law will not touch
wants.text_restrained: wants a wrong set right that the law will not touch

bonds.text: still carries a loss no one is allowed to mention
keeps returning to a ruin that no one else remembers
would answer the call of one particular old ship

slots.prompt: Pick the place that raised you.

options.title: Waterside
options.text: Your cradle was planking and your lullaby was water on hull. You still wake before the tide turns, and your hand goes looking for a rope.

options.title: Highland and stone
options.text: Wind, rock and long silences. You learned to read weather in the colour of a cliff, and to save your voice for the moments that needed it.

options.title: Town and market
options.text: Everyone's business was everyone's business. You grew up counting change, reading faces, and knowing which doors stayed open after dark.

options.title: On the road
options.text: You never slept in the same bed twice. Wheels, hooves and strangers' fires were home, and saying goodbye was a skill you practised early.

options.title: Shrine and cloister
options.text: Bells before dawn, floors scrubbed by hand, and a great many rules nobody would explain. You kept most of them, and some you still keep in your sleep.

options.title: Great house
options.text: You knew the great house from its wrong end: cellars, back stairs, and what was said when no one thought you listened. Standing or ruined, it still has your keys.

options.title: Forest and fell
options.text: The trees closed over your childhood like a lid. You knew birdsong before letters, and how to walk without a sound, because something was always listening.

options.title: Under the city
options.text: A city has a basement, and you were raised in it: drains, tanneries, rooftops, the hours no watchman keeps. Light was something other people owned.

options.title: Parents and kin
options.text: Someone of your own blood raised you, with more love than money. Their sayings still turn up in your mouth when you are tired or afraid.

options.title: The street and neighbours
options.text: No single hand raised you. The whole lane did, each keeping a different part of you alive. You owe a baker, a cobbler and a woman nobody names.

options.title: A temple or a master
options.text: One teacher shaped you, in a cell or a workshop or a cold lecture room. Praise was rare and exact, and you can still hear the corrections.

options.title: A garrison or a ship's crew
options.text: Barracks bunks or a swaying hammock, drum-calls and a rule for everything. They looked after you the way soldiers look after tools: thoroughly, and without sentiment.

options.title: Wanderers
options.text: A troupe, a caravan, a band on the move. You were passed between laps and wagon seats, and taught tricks, tunes and the right face for a toll-keeper.

options.title: On your own, or in the wild
options.text: Nobody raised you in particular. You raised yourself on what could be snared, begged or borrowed, and learned early that you could not afford to be told twice.

options.title: A guild or workshop
options.text: You grew up between a bench and a bed in the back of a workshop, paid in food and lessons. The master's rules were hard, and so was their hand, and you are good at the work.

options.title: Taken in
options.text: You were no one's, until someone made you theirs: a farmer's widow, a ferryman, a priest with a spare cot. You still don't know what you did to deserve it.

stages.title: What you did for a living
stages.question: Who were you before?

slots.prompt: Pick the kind of work. Then pick the trade (jobs.json).

options.title: Arms and guard
options.text: You stood a post for wages: gate, wall, quarry or caravan. Long hours of boredom with a few minutes of fear in them taught you to spot trouble before it spoke.

options.title: Road and river
options.text: You moved goods and people from one place to another, by barge, cart or on foot. You know ferrymen's gossip, stable-yard prices and which bridges are rotten.

options.title: Shadow and street
options.text: You worked the margins of a town: lamps and tunes, back-door deals and quick fingers. Most people look past you, and you have found that useful.

options.title: Faith and healing
options.text: You tended the sick, the hives, the bells or the lamp before a shrine. The work was gentle and relentless, and it showed you how people behave in their worst hour.

options.title: Books and ledgers
options.text: You lived among ink, tallies and shelves. Someone had to know what was owed, what was written and what had quietly been scraped out, and for years that was you.

options.title: Craft and field
options.text: Your hands learned a trade or a harvest: nets, stone, thread, furrows. Good work is its own kind of quiet, and you know what a day of it does to a body.

options.title: A loss
options.text: You lost people, or a home, to fever or flood, and learned that grief is also work that somebody has to do. Mostly you did it alone.

options.title: A disaster survived
options.text: Fire took the guildhall, or every bell in town rang with no hand on a rope. You were there. Certain smells and sounds still bring the night back whole.

options.title: War at the edge
options.text: A border skirmish went through you like weather. You saw what steel does to people who were singing that morning, and walked away with only the sound of it.
options.text_restrained: A border skirmish swept past you like weather. You saw how quickly a quiet field turns, and walked away with only the sound of it.

options.title: A calling or a lesson
options.text: You walked a long pilgrim road, or learned your letters from a widow who asked only that you teach another. Either way you came back different, and a little more careful.

options.title: A debt of kindness
options.text: A stranger took you in out of a storm, or you returned a purse you could have kept. Either kindness cost something and paid something back. You still keep that account.

options.title: A hard master or a long walk
options.text: At twelve you were sent to a master who never smiled, or at fifteen you walked alone to a distant city. Either road taught you how much you can carry without saying so.

options.title: A small triumph
options.text: You won a race that mattered to a whole village, or fed a hundred people from almost nothing. For one day you were somebody, and you have been chasing or dodging that feeling since.

options.title: A friendship broken
options.text: You watched an old friendship end over a few words, or you were sold out by someone you trusted. The wound closed. The habit of watching hands stayed.

options.title: A killing
options.text: You killed someone, and it was not a fair fight. You have told the story three ways. None of them is the whole truth, and the dead do not argue.
options.text_restrained: You hurt someone badly, and it was not a fair fight. You have told the story three ways. None of them is the whole truth.

options.title: A village burned
options.text: You watched a village burn, and counted the bodies in the road because you could not stop counting. You were too far away to help and too close to forget.
options.text_restrained: You watched a village burn from a hillside, and counted the roofs because you could not stop counting. You were too far away to help and too close to forget.

stages.title: How you learned to fight or cast
stages.question: How do you fight?

slots.prompt: Pick how you came by your skill.

options.title: Drilled in a formation
options.text: You learned to fight shoulder to shoulder, where holding your place mattered more than winning the exchange. A sergeant's voice still moves your feet.

options.title: Learned to shoot straight
options.text: A bow, a target and a stubborn teacher. You learned to breathe out, wait for the wind to pause, and loose before you felt sure. Mostly you were right.

options.title: Fury and endurance
options.text: Something in you does not stop when it should. You learned to trust the red tide, to hit through pain, and to remember afterwards only the sound.

options.title: Quiet blades and shadows
options.text: You learned to be where no one was looking: locks, shadows, the one loose stair, and a knife kept for the day quiet fails.

options.title: Prayer and vows
options.text: You learned by vow and candle: long kneeling hours, hard promises, and the discovery that faith can be held like a shield and swung like a hammer.

options.title: Study and spellbooks
options.text: Cold rooms, bad light and books that argued with each other. You learned that power is mostly preparation, and that the dangerous page is the one you skipped.

options.title: The hunt and the wild
options.text: You learned by following: broken twigs, cold ashes, the way a hare sits when it knows. Hunger was a good teacher, and so was whatever hunted you back.

options.title: Song and story
options.text: You learned in taverns and at hearths, from people who could hold a room with a pause. Names, tunes and a hundred old tales are your weapons, and memory is your armour.

options.title: Inner discipline
options.text: Breath, balance and a thousand repetitions. Someone made you hold a stance until your legs shook, then told you the shaking was the lesson.

options.title: A gift in the blood
options.text: The power was never taught; it arrived. A flicker when you were angry, a hum when you were afraid, and the slow, uneasy understanding that it is yours.

options.title: A bargain with something
options.text: You asked for something in the dark, and something answered. The terms sounded generous, the signature was yours, and the other party has never once forgotten.
options.text_restrained: You asked for help in the dark, and something answered. The terms sounded generous, and the other party has never once forgotten them.

options.title: The wild's own magic
options.text: The old places taught you, not people: stone circles, spring water, the long breath of a forest. You listen before you act, and the land sometimes answers.

options.title: To clear a debt
options.text: There is a debt, in coin or in kindness, and it sits on your chest at night. You mean to clear it before it clears you.

options.title: To find someone
options.text: Someone is missing: a sibling, a teacher, a friend who stopped writing. You carry their last words like a coin you won't spend, and ask every stranger the same question.

options.title: To earn a name
options.text: You want your name said in rooms you have never entered, with respect, by people who need not be polite. You are patient about it. You are also not a patient person.

options.title: To protect a place or people
options.text: Somewhere is yours to keep safe: a street, a mill, a ferry crossing. You will stand in the road for it, and you have already thought about what that costs.

options.title: To leave the past behind
options.text: You want to stop running. You want to wake in one place twice in a row and not check the door. First you must do something about whatever is following you.

options.title: To understand a mystery
options.text: A question has hold of you: a locked room, a missing page, a story that does not add up. You will follow it somewhere unwise just to see how it ends.

options.title: To see a rival brought low
options.text: One face keeps coming back, smiling. You don't need them dead. You need to watch their certainty crack, and to be standing close when it does.

options.title: To make someone pay
options.text: Someone took something from you, and the law will not collect it. You keep a list with one name on it, and you have kept it short on purpose.
options.text_restrained: Someone took something from you, and the law will not set it right. You keep a list with one name on it, and your patience is not endless.

stages.title: Who you are tied to
stages.question: Who or what are you tied to?

second_kind.note: On a 5 or 6 roll the kind table again and keep a different kind.

options.title: A younger sibling
options.text: A younger brother or sister who still thinks you can fix anything. You send what you can and lie about how you earned it.

options.title: An old teacher
options.text: A teacher who saw something in you before you did and never said so aloud. When you hesitate, you hear their voice.

options.title: A comrade
options.text: A comrade whose back you guarded, and who guarded yours. Living or dead, you made them a promise, and you intend to keep it.

options.title: A rival
options.text: A rival who has measured themselves against you for years. If you fell, they would pick you up and complain about it the whole way home.

options.title: A lost love
options.text: Someone you loved, and lost to distance or death or your own pride. You do not speak of them. In crowds, you notice anyone who walks the way they did.

options.title: A parent growing old
options.text: A parent whose hands are slowing. The letters from home are shorter each year, and you read them twice before you sleep.

options.title: The home town
options.text: Bread smoke, wet slate, one crooked clock everyone ignores. You would crawl back to it, if it came to that.

options.title: A ruin
options.text: A ruin you cannot stay away from: the broken stair, the cold hearth, the wall with a hand printed in soot. Someone should remember what stood there.

options.title: A ship
options.text: A ship, or the memory of one: the creak of her ribs, the beat of the pumps, the smell of tar. If she ever called, you would answer.

options.title: A shrine
options.text: A small shrine you tend out of habit: fresh water, a pinch of salt, a word. You don't know whether anyone listens. You would feel it if you stopped.

options.title: A garden
options.text: A plot, a row of beans that wants water at dawn wherever else life leads. A neighbour has your key. You think about those beans more than you would admit.

options.title: A supper table
options.text: A table in a noisy kitchen where a seat is always kept for you, and a plate set. It is the nearest thing you have to proof that you belong somewhere.

options.title: You owe a person
options.text: You owe someone more than money: a life, a lie they kept for you, a night's shelter that cost them dearly. You mean to repay it exactly, and in full.

options.title: You owe a guild
options.text: A guild paid for your training and expects its years back, with interest. The ledger is longer than your patience, and its collectors are always polite.

options.title: You owe a temple
options.text: A temple fed you through a bad winter and keeps your name in a book. They have never asked for repayment, which is exactly why you cannot stop thinking about it.

options.title: A person owes you
options.text: Someone owes you: coin, an apology, a favour that cost you dear. They have not forgotten. They are waiting to see whether you will make them say it.

options.title: A guild owes you
options.text: A guild owes you wages, or credit, or your name on a piece of work. They hope you will let it lapse. You have kept the papers, and the memory of who signed.

options.title: A temple owes you
options.text: A temple promised you something when you were at your lowest, and the promise went quiet. Maybe the priest died. Maybe they simply stopped answering.

options.title: A captain who sold you out
options.text: A captain gave you up to save their own neck and watched you go over the side. You have a good memory for faces and a longer one for the names of ships.

options.title: A creditor who took everything
options.text: A creditor took the house, the tools and the cart in a single afternoon and called it business. You can still recite the clerk's phrasing.

options.title: A former master
options.text: A former master worked you hard and hit you harder, and told the world you were lazy. You see their kind everywhere, and your jaw tightens.
options.text_restrained: A former master worked you hard and spoke you down, and told the world you were lazy. You see their kind everywhere, and your jaw tightens.

options.title: A comrade you left behind
options.text: You left a comrade behind on a bad day and told yourself it was the only choice. They survived. You have not stopped listening for the news.

options.title: A family you ruined
options.text: A family you ruined, through a lie or a debt or one careless word. They did not deserve it. When you hear their name, your next breath comes late.

options.title: An innocent you blamed
options.text: You put your own fault on someone else to save yourself, and they paid for it. They know the truth. You wonder what they have made of it.

stages.title: A flaw, a secret, a fear
stages.question: What do you hide?

options.title: A gambler
options.text: You cannot walk past a game of chance. The dice have your name on them, you swear, and by the second round you almost believe it.

options.title: A boaster
options.text: You tell your exploits loud and bright, and a good half of them belonged to someone else. When silence comes, you fill it with the next story.

options.title: A grudge-keeper
options.text: You never forgive a slight. You make no plans; you simply remember every one, in perfect order, and each one sits in your gut, cold and exact.

options.title: Hot-tempered
options.text: When you are hurried, your temper bites first and thinks afterwards. You have broken more than one door, and apologised for fewer than you should.

options.title: A fibber
options.text: Small lies keep your life interesting: a titled uncle, a famous teacher. Nobody is hurt by them, until the day somebody checks.

options.title: Too proud
options.text: You cannot take help. You would carry a fallen wall on your back before you asked a neighbour to hold the other end.

options.title: A meddler
options.text: You cannot leave a secret alone. A closed door is an insult, a sealed letter a challenge, and other people's business your favourite pastime.

options.title: A pilferer
options.text: Small things find their way into your pockets: a spoon, a button, a pinch from the common purse. You always mean to give them back.

options.title: A crime
options.text: There is a crime in your past that no court ever heard of. You were never caught, and on some nights you wish you had been.

options.title: A broken oath
options.text: You swore an oath on something sacred and then broke it. Nobody else knows the words you used, or which of them you chose to betray.

options.title: A lie I told
options.text: You told a lie that other people have since built on. If it cracked, a good deal would fall. You tend it carefully, like a wall you built crooked.

options.title: A dangerous debt
options.text: You owe something to someone you should never have borrowed from. They have been patient so far. Patience is a loan, too.

options.title: A thing I carry
options.text: You carry something you should have given up or handed over: a letter, a ring, a key. You never open it. You never put it down.

options.title: A belief about my birth
options.text: You believe your birth was not what you were told: another name, a grander house, or a darker one. You have no proof, only a feeling that will not leave.

options.title: Deep water
options.text: Deep water. Whether or not you can swim, the dark underneath turns your knees to wet rope.

options.title: Fire in the night
options.text: Fire in the night. The light comes first, then the sound, and your body is running for the door before your mind has said why.

options.title: Failing others
options.text: Failing the people who rely on you. You have rehearsed it in the dark so many times that it feels like a memory.

options.title: The dark
options.text: The thick dark with no edges. You sleep with a candle burning and tell everyone it is thrift.

options.title: Being forgotten
options.text: Being forgotten. Not killed: forgotten, your name worn smooth as a pilgrim's step until even you cannot read it.

options.title: Crowds
options.text: Crowds. All those elbows, all that breath, and nowhere to put your back. You manage fine, right up until you don't.

follow_ups.question: What did the work teach you?
follow_ups.when: The chosen trade belongs to a weak job family (craft-and-field), or the top two background weights tie after stage 3, or a free-text story names two trades that disagree.

follow_ups.question: Which of these sounds most like you?
follow_ups.when: The top two class weights tie after stage 5. Options are the stage-5 cards of the tied classes; if stage 5 was never answered, the six featured stage-5 cards.

follow_ups.question: At arm's length, or up close?
follow_ups.when: The class is Fighter (the only class with a Fighting Style feature at level 1 in the SRD set). Asked after stage 5.

options.label: One heavy swing at a time

follow_ups.question: Did you fight more than you healed, or the reverse?
follow_ups.when: The class is Cleric (Divine Order) or Druid (Primal Order).

follow_ups.question: Is this a rumour your hero believes, a lie they tell, or a daydream?
follow_ups.when: The record holds a claim (title, rank, wealth, an item or a relationship) taken from a secret card or free text. A claim never grants anything.

follow_ups.question: Let the story bring your past into play?
follow_ups.when: The last card of creation. Shown unchecked; skipping counts as 'not-yet'.
